clue.text: To shock part of Birmingham is hard

parts.note: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa football club
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by how tough one district of Birmingham is.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTON is an inner-city district of Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to give them a sudden jolt of surprise, a synonym of shock.

clue.text: A piano's bell-like sound offering some attraction

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a peal is the ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A piano rings out like a bell, making it rather appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, 'softly', in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is the quality of attracting interest or liking, a synonym of attraction.

clue.text: Commits crime on less than half of these beats

indicators.note: less than half of a five-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: robs means commits theft, a crime

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the law on a portion of these rhythms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half of these' takes TH, two of its five letters, placed after ROBS.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulsing beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Admiral, leader of navy one's left at sea

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
at sea means confused, so the letters of one's and the left abbreviation are jumbled

explanation.surface: An admiral heads the navy while one man is left adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles ONES and L to ELSON, after N, the first letter of 'navy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio, Lord Nelson was the British naval admiral who won at Trafalgar.

clue.text: Sea turning rough, moving idly

indicators.note: a rough sea is choppy and churned, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: The sea becomes choppy while drifting along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SEA TURNING, ten letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to stroll in a leisurely way, walking without hurry.

clue.text: Fellow meeting difficulty after beginning to carve one small angel

indicators.note: the beginning of the word carve is its opening letter

parts.note: a fellow is a man, he
rub means a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A man runs into trouble just after starting to sculpt a little angel figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places HE and RUB after the C taken from 'beginning to carve'. RUB is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are the chubby winged infants of religious art, the smallest kind of angel figure.

clue.text: Family relic, one found in that woman's tower?

indicators.note: found in means the numeral sits inside the word for that woman's

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
to tower over something is to loom over it

explanation.surface: A family keepsake turned up in a woman's tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' reads as a building, but here it is the verb: to tower is to LOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object passed down through the generations of a family.

clue.text: Hold revolutionary skills in feature of horsemanship

indicators.note: the turned-round skills go in the rein

parts.note: a rein is part of the gear a rider uses to control a horse

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for skills is read backwards

parts.note: arts are skills

explanation.surface: Rebel skills are restrained in horse riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ARTS round to STRA, which goes 'in' REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to keep in check, to hold back.

clue.text: Wave around a cereal container

parts.note: bran is a cereal husk eaten at breakfast
a dish is a container for food

explanation.surface: Waving about a breakfast bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave around a cereal container' reads as one picture; the definition is just 'Wave around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish something is to flourish it threateningly, waving it about.

clue.text: What could it be in our piles in quake?

definitions.text: What could it be in our piles in quake?

indicators.note: a quake shakes things, so the letters of our piles are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking how dangerous our heaps of belongings would be in an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in quake' shakes OUR PILES into the answer, and the whole clue is also the definition: piles in an earthquake are in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps caught in an earthquake are in danger of toppling, which is what a hazardous state is.

clue.text: Shame on you, having curtailed brilliant carnival

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation meaning shame on you

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut, so the word for brilliant loses its last letter

parts.note: a brilliant performer is a star

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a dazzling performer whose carnival act was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the last letter from STAR, leaving STA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a Spanish-style public festival, a celebration much like a carnival.

clue.text: A recipe — Cullen Skink? — passed round a Scottish town

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin recipe on prescriptions

indicators.note: the soup is passed round the second a, enclosing it

parts.note: Cullen skink is a Scottish soup of smoked haddock, so a broth

explanation.surface: A bowl of Cullen skink is handed round a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cullen skink is a thick Scottish smoked-haddock soup; 'passed round' puts BROTH round the second A to make BROATH. Arbroath is famous for its smoked haddock, the Arbroath smokie.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbroath is a fishing town on the Angus coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Very ornate but incomplete state

indicators.note: incomplete means the state's name is left without its final letter

parts.note: Florida is a US state

explanation.surface: Something is called over-decorated yet unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last A from FLORIDA. 'state' looks like a condition, but it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid describes elaborate, flowery decoration or prose, heavily embellished.

clue.text: Scores victories, capturing King — time for a nap?

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two scores make forty

indicators.note: capturing means the victories hold the king's letter inside

parts.note: wins are victories
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player racks up wins, takes the king, and then naps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like a verb, but it is two scores, or forty; 'capturing' puts K inside WINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleep during the day is a doze, the idiom being forty winks.

clue.text: Study of work patterns since groom is upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of since groom are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a workplace study happened because the groom got upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SINCE GROOM, ten letters, into the answer; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics is the science of designing workplaces and tasks around how people actually work.

clue.text: Father, with the nervous affliction, is deserving of pity

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A dad with a twitch is pitiable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means arousing sympathy or sorrow, so pitiable.

clue.text: Naughty mischievous child climbing on cowboy?

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a cowboy ropes cattle, so is a roper

explanation.surface: A naughty brat clambers on a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'climbing on' puts IMP above ROPER. The question mark flags that a roper is a cowboy only by job description.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means rude or indecent, as in a naughty remark.

clue.text: Some plan should be sorted out for redundancy

indicators.note: sorted out means put into order, so the letters of some plan are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan should be devised to deal with job losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redundancy' suggests job losses; it is the use of superfluous words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleonasm is the use of more words than needed, a verbal surplus.

clue.text: Where to keep unwanted things

parts.note: reads as a storage place, such as a loft, but means the distance at which one holds people or matters one wishes to avoid

explanation.surface: Asking about a storage spot for junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests an attic or cupboard; it means keeping something away from you, at a distance the length of an extended limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something at a distance means not getting close to it, the idiom for avoiding involvement.

clue.text: Keep supporting live act

indicators.note: in a down answer supporting means the second piece is underneath the first

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
to have is to keep or possess

explanation.surface: Continue backing a live performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' looks like a stage turn; it is the verb, to conduct oneself. In a down answer HAVE 'supporting' BE sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to conduct oneself, which is how one acts.

clue.text: A vote over start of organised space mission

indicators.note: in a down answer over means the earlier pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: a poll is a vote

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A ballot held over the beginning of a planned space flight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer A POLL sits 'over' O, the first letter of 'organised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the NASA programme that landed astronauts on the Moon.

clue.text: 3, perhaps, capturing Arab man

indicators.note: capturing means the wrestling grip holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: the answer to 3 down is also a wrestling grip, so it is an example of a hold
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An admiral seizes an Arab man.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the admiral at 3 down, but here it is the wrestling hold of the same name; 'capturing' puts AR inside HOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold is a man's first name.

clue.text: Hour in which soldiers run out in fear

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces go inside the word for hour
out means the letter U is thrown out of the word hour

parts.note: taken as written
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dreadful hour in which troops flee in panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes U from HOUR, leaving HOR; 'in which' puts OR (other ranks) and R (run) inside after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense dread or terror, a strong form of fear.

clue.text: Petals not left scattered round little flower

indicators.note: round means the scattered letters go around the word for little
scattered means the remaining letters are strewn into a new order
not means the letter for left is omitted from petals

parts.note: wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: Petals strewn around a small flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not left' removes L from PETALS; 'scattered' rearranges PETAS to S...TPEA, which goes 'round' WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden plant grown for its fragrant blooms.

clue.text: Astaire film that will involve work

indicators.note: involve means take inside, so the word that encloses the abbreviation for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Fred Astaire movie that is going to need effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will involve' puts OP (opus, a work) inside THAT. Top Hat (1935) is a Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is the 1935 musical starring Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers.

clue.text: Pin this artwork as representation of oil-painting?

indicators.note: representation suggests the letters of the painting are rearranged, with pin plus the answer made from them

explanation.surface: Pinning up a picture as a depiction of an oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: PIN plus the answer together use exactly the letters of OIL-PAINTING, as 'as representation of' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a design engraved or incised into a surface, a kind of carved or printed artwork.

clue.text: Church — the Catholic one? It offers reflection

parts.note: the Roman Catholic Church is the church of Rome

explanation.surface: Asking whether a church is the Catholic one, as it gives food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' suggests contemplation in church; it is a shiny surface that reflects light.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome plating gives a bright mirror-like finish that reflects light.

clue.text: A sex hormone producing heavenly body

parts.note: sex hormones such as testosterone are steroids

explanation.surface: A hormone gives rise to a celestial object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' could suggest an attractive physique, which a hormone might produce; here it is a rock in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are rocky bodies orbiting the Sun, objects in the heavens.
